⛈️ APOC Weather Engine v25

Deterministic fantasy weather · one file · works offline Seed — 52 weathers · 6 categories

Generate rolls a fresh seed every click, so the weather changes every time — and the seed shown up top always reproduces the result on screen exactly (share links too). Shortcuts: G generate · N next day · F focus

Calendar — Faerûn

The seed is the only randomness. Change it for a different roll on the same date.

Climate & Odds

Weights are relative shares — the % shown is each category's real chance per roll. Defaults add up to a clean 100. (v1 hid Calm as a ~2% leftover; here it is an honest slider.)

Freezing rule (Auto temperature): rain at ≤35°F falls as snow, snow above 35°F falls as rain.

Scene & Saving

Settings and history save on this device automatically. Animation pauses when the tab is hidden or your system asks for reduced motion.

APOC Weather Engine v25 — rebuilt 2026. All 52 subtype descriptions and the Faerûn calendar are carried over verbatim from the original. v25 (Shaun, 2026-11-07): DM WORKSPACE — the movable-pieces treatment and in-place text editing are DM-ONLY: this page arms DM mode per device from the DM link (…?dm=1); everyone else gets the clean stock page with no grips, handles, locks or editing. In DM mode, framing text (labels, headings, hints, button names) can be reworded in place behind the Editing lock (default locked); generated weather values and the scene artwork are never editable. Layout and wording save on the DM’s device only. v24 (Shaun, 2026-11-07): MOVABLE PIECES — every panel, section and card on the page can be dragged by its ⠿ grip, resized from any edge or corner, flipped vertical/horizontal by its shape, and locked in place piece by piece. Layout saves on this device only; ↺ Reset Layout in the header restores the shipped arrangement. v23 (Shaun, 2026-10-31): HATE STORMS CARRY THEIR OWN TEMPERATURE. v22 left a hatestorm's temperature blank unless set by hand — Shaun's ruling: blank is wrong; the storm itself sets the temperature. Each of the 19 hatestorms now rolls its temperature from its own nature, in any month of the year: a Firestorm runs 110–150°F, Green Rain steams at 85–110°F, Rain of Blood falls warm at 70–90°F, while Frozen Ruin plunges to −10–15°F, Howl of the North bites at 0–25°F, and the snow-born storms (Blood Snow Blizzard, Negation Flurry, Razor Sleet, Rust Flurry) stay below freezing. The climate-shift slider still applies on top, and a temperature set by hand still wins. The season half of v22 stands unchanged: no hatestorm is ever stamped with the month's season. v22 (Shaun, 2026-10-31): HATE STORMS ANSWER TO NO CALENDAR — a hatestorm is not month-, season- or weather-dependent. Its odds stay the flat slider in every month of the year, a rolled hatestorm is no longer stamped with the month-derived season, and it no longer borrows the month's temperature (a Firestorm in Hammer used to present at Deepwinter's 10°F). A side benefit: a winter hatestorm's ground now renders in the storm's own bruised dark instead of winter white. Every other weather keeps its seasons and month temperatures as before. Built on v21, which completed the subtype-art program: all 52 weathers have a distinct treatment — 37 own artwork + 15 graded variants. v9 starts the full set: every subtype gets its own picture, rolled out in batches (plan: SUBTYPE-ART-PLAN.md). The engine now looks up a picture by subtype first and falls back to the category scene until a subtype's art lands. Same v20, Shaun's five calls (2026-10-31). STRIPES FIXED: the permanent mist was drawn as four flat rectangles with hard top and bottom edges — stripes running through every scene, worst in Fog where they were thickest — and the graded variants' washes seamed hard mid-frame. The mist is still there (this world is always foggy) but every band and wash now fades through a gradient; all 134 pictures in the art folder were surveyed by eye and by pixel measurement, and the stripes were never in the art, only in the overlays drawn on top of it. LIGHTNING, A TAD LESS: the Hatestorm screen-flash fires ~40% less often and at .45 alpha instead of .75; Magnetic Storm's static runs fewer and dimmer. VARIATIONS: every weather type now cycles three pattern variants of its own — Fog: banks, rolling banks, creeping ground fog. Rain: steady, gusting sheets, fine drizzle. Snow: calm fall, swirling, driving. Rare: sparks drifting, swirling, rising. Calm: still, faint wisps, low haze — picked per roll from the seed. HATE STORMS GET UNIQUE (Shaun: 'get crazy'): all 19 run their own animated treatment matched to their description — black hail pellets hammer down, the Howl streams sideways as visible wind, Negation Flurry glints as it dispels, Nettles fall as tumbling thorn-specks, Crushing Darkness breathes, Reverse Rain finally falls UP — and five hate storms get their own artwork at last (Magnetic Storm, Acid Rain, Death Hail, Blood Snow Blizzard, Necroburst): 35 of 52 weathers now have their own picture, 6 graded variants remain, 41 of 52 get a distinct treatment. The generator still declined Rain of Blood, Rain of Frogs or Fish and Firestorm; they keep graded scenes under their new animated treatments. GUI THEMING: the interface dresses for the weather on display — murk green Fog, steel-blue Rain, ice-pale Snow, arcane-violet Rare, bruised ember Hatestorm — crossfading over .8s; the scene art still obeys the Fog of Life. Batch 11 (v21) COMPLETES THE SET — all 52 subtypes now have a distinct treatment. New artwork: Dead Calm and Perfect Stillness close out Calm (8/8, the fifth complete category); Incorporeal Wind (spectral currents streaming through solid walls), Rogue Zephyr (one playful ribbon of breeze in a still valley), Arcane Tempest (multicoloured lightning, raw magic arcs), Dragon's Breath (flame wisps curling out of the ground mist) and Aberrant Sky (the grey itself twisted into an impossible spiral). The generator declined Ghoststorm, Undead Fog, Gale Force Winds and Skyquake, so those four take bespoke graded variants over the fog scene. Final tally: 37 own artwork + 15 graded variants = 52 of 52. Batch 10 (v20) was a correction, not new art: a routing audit against the engine's own data caught that four portraits painted this round (Still Day, Weird Calm, Golden Fog, Gloom) were names from working notes, NOT among the 52 subtypes in the data — they were unreachable and have been removed from the file (the paintings are kept in the art folder, unassigned). Standing after the five calls above: 41 of 52 distinct treatments — 35 own artwork + 6 graded variants. Still to do (11): Dead Calm and Perfect Stillness close out Calm; all 9 Rare weathers remain. Batch 9 (v19) worked the Calm sky: Dark Foreboding Sky (a churning near-black ceiling, nothing falling — pure dread) and High Gray Sky (the cloud deck lifted high, ridges visible, the longest view this world gives) get their own artwork. The generator declined Harsh Seasonal Winds and Typical Day, so both take graded variants over the valley fog scene — streaming wind grade for the one, a barely-there neutral grade for the other (a typical day should look like the valley itself). 41 of 52 distinct treatments — 30 own artwork + 11 graded variants. Now published live — every build pushes straight to the site. Batch 8 (v18): Small Hail (pea-sized pellets rattling off the roofs) and Large Hail (baseball-sized stones, the cottage roof stove in, hail drifted against the tower) finish the SNOW family — 6 for 6, the third complete category. Plus the first two Calm portraits: Very Light Winds (mist drifting at a crawl, one smoke ribbon leaning) and Clear-ish Day (the clearest day this world allows — pale grey veil, mountain ghosts, still no sun). 37 of 52 distinct treatments — 28 own artwork + 9 graded variants. Batch 7 (v17) climbed the Snow ladder: Light Snow (sparse drifting flakes, the valley calm and visible), Heavy Snow (the path buried, drifts at the walls, endless still snowfall) and Whiteout (a wind-scoured wall of white, the cottage corner at arm's reach — Solid Fog's twin). The generator declined Blizzard, so it takes the graded route: a white blast grade over the Howl of the North artwork, which already had the wind. 33 of 52 distinct treatments — 24 own artwork + 9 graded variants. Batch 6 (v16) completed the Rain family: Light Rain (fine drizzle, rippling puddles, mist), Heavy Rain (mud-slick path, water sheeting off the roofs), Downpour (a solid curtain of water, the path flooded mirror-flat) and Thunderstorm (gusting diagonal rain, lightning blooming diffusely through the fog behind the tower) — with Reverse Rain the family is 5 for 5, the second complete category after Fog. 29 of 52 distinct treatments — 21 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 5 (v15), a clean sweep — all four accepted: Rust Flurry (rust-flecked flakes, corroding iron), Acid Sleet (slanting chemical sleet, bubbling acid puddles), Green Rain (emerald downpour, steaming green channels) and Reverse Rain (water streaming UP off the path into the sky — the impossible one, nailed). 25 of 52 distinct treatments — 17 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 4 (v14): Howl of the North (the wind made visible, snow streaming sideways), Negation Flurry (serene silvery snow, dispelling sparkles) and Razor Sleet (ice shards slanting, every surface rimed in crystal blades) got their own artwork. The generator declined Death Hail, so it takes the graded route: negative-energy gloom over the snow scene, black hail pellets falling dark. 21 of 52 distinct treatments — 13 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 3 (v13): Frozen Ruin (the valley flash-frozen, icicle eaves, mirror-ice floor) and Crushing Darkness (purple-black evil twilight, one smothered window) got their own artwork. The generator declined Magnetic Storm and Blood Snow Blizzard, so both take the graded route Shaun chose: Magnetic Storm = violet electrical gloom over the storm scene with pale static-spark particles; Blood Snow Blizzard = crimson grade over the snow scene with red snowfall. 17 of 52 distinct treatments — 10 own artwork + 7 graded variants. v12 completed the Fog family in the Bastion aesthetic (Shaun's reference streets, 2026-10-28): Light Fog (treeline ghosted, quarter-mile), Heavy Fog (lamp-halos in the murk, 500 ft), Dense Fog (tower a looming shape, 100 ft), Solid Fog (a wall of vapor, cottage corner at arm's reach, 5 ft) — with Crimson Fog the whole family is done. A Bastion city-street scene set comes later, by Shaun's word. 13 of 52 have a distinct treatment — 8 own artwork + 5 engine-graded variants. v11 gave the five generator-refused storms their graded variants (Shaun's pick): Rain of Blood (deep crimson grade, blood-red rain), Firestorm (smoke and ember-orange grade, rising embers), Acid Rain (chartreuse burn grade, acid-green streaks), Necroburst (black-green necrotic gloom), Rain of Frogs or Fish (drowned teal grade, tumbling falling silhouettes). 9 of 52 now have a distinct treatment — 4 own artwork + 5 graded variants. Batch 2: Violet Rain joins (violet downpour over a world drained of colour — dead magic) — 4 of 52 have their own art. The generator refused Acid Rain, Rain of Frogs or Fish and Necroburst, as it did Rain of Blood and Firestorm in batch 1; those five wait on Shaun's call (engine-graded variants, or reference photos like the Nettles one). Batch 1: Green Fog (luminous green murk, buildings drowning in it) and Crimson Fog (sight cut to a few feet of red) join Plague of Nettles — 3 of 52 have their own art. v8 adds the first subtype-specific artwork: Plague of Nettles rolls its own scene, built to Shaun's reference photo — the cottage and tower completely encased in a skin of foliage, no bare wood or stone, growth on every surface, flowering plants of all colours threaded through the green, under the same flat grey sky. It crossfades in like every scene change; at night the night scene still wins. v7 fixes the odds: the rebuild had set Calm to 60% of all rolls, burying everything else — your original script's math was Hatestorm 10, Rare 5, Snow 5, Rain 10, Fog 10 out of 41, with Calm as the 1-in-41 remainder (~2%). Those exact percentages are restored (the Calm slider now defaults to 1, so the readouts show the true shares). Saved settings reset once in v7 so the bad 60% saved in your browser doesn't follow you; your own slider changes persist from here. Hatestorm is the biggest family — 19 of the 52 — so at ~24% of rolls you'll see its kinds regularly. v6: full re-audit (data byte-identical to v1, no dead references, calendar boundary / manual / off-mode / weights / share-link tests all green) plus better visuals — Snow and Rare have their own grey-world artwork now (every category covered), photos crossfade through the fog instead of cutting, a permanent drifting mist layer sits over every scene (it is always foggy to some degree), and share links now carry temperature, season, time and wind so they reproduce a result exactly on any machine. v5 fixes: Generate now rolls a fresh seed on every click (in v2–v4 it re-rolled the same seed, so the result never changed and the button looked dead), and a Focus button (or the F key) minimises everything except the result. World canon (Shaun, 2026-10-28): the Fog of Life fills the world all the way out to the scarred crystal sphere — there is no visible sun, no moon, no stars; the sky is always grey, or worse; it simply gets light, then dark. v4 rebuilds every scene on that rule. New in v3: photorealistic AI artwork embedded in the file — the same valley, cottage and tower under Calm, Fog, Rain and Hatestorm skies, with time-of-day grading, subtype tint and live particles over the photo. Snow and Rare ride the closest photo under heavy grading until their own artwork batch lands; if a photo ever fails, the procedural scene takes over. Fixes vs. v1: no missing photos/ folder (the scene is 100% procedural, so the file truly works alone) · one seeded roll for weather and scene (v1 rolled the weather with pure chance, so share links could not reproduce it) · Auto / Manual / Off per field instead of the linked/unlinked toggle maze · settings persist · day is clamped to the month (v1 allowed day 40) · lighter canvas (particle caps, pauses off-screen, honours reduced-motion).
